submitted.rationale: EQE rose steadily with Fe content: 0.015% at index 14 (Fe0.48), 0.052% at index 2 (Fe0.80) and 0.077% at index 0 (Fe0.84). Index 0 is the most Fe-rich composition in the library. MACE puts hematite on the hull, and MEGNet predicts a 2.77 eV gap, so it absorbs at 3.2 eV. Sb-rich films look worse.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.015%. Rutile FeSbO4 is stable per MACE (0.0016 eV/atom above hull) but gives low EQE.
Not measured. EQE fell as Sb increased, and Sb oxides have wide gaps.

consultations.verdict: Support (weak): MEGNet HSE gaps for rutile FeSbO4 (2.08 eV) and hematite (2.77 eV) are both below the 3.2 eV photon energy, so either phase can absorb. Fe-rich index 2 (Fe0.80) should be mostly Sb-modified Fe2O3 with some FeSbO4, a plausible photoactive mix. I'm measuring it first to anchor the Fe-rich end of the line.

Support: MACE puts rutile FeSbO4 only 0.0016 eV/atom above the hull, so it should form as a single phase near Fe:Sb = 1:1 (index 14, Fe0.48). Its predicted gap of 2.08 eV absorbs at 3.2 eV. The Fe-rich index 2 was poor (0.052%), so testing the stable ternary phase is the logical next step.

Support (moderate): MACE puts hematite on the hull (0.0 eV/atom), and its predicted gap of 2.77 eV absorbs at 3.2 eV. EQE fell from 0.052% at Fe0.80 to 0.015% at Fe0.48, so more hematite-like, Fe-rich films look better. Index 0 (Fe0.84) is the most Fe-rich composition in the library.
